author_version.question: As known at mark before-denial, are d1 and d2, d2 and d3, d3 and d4 the same, and is d1 (Kestrel-4) a member of the North Survey Fleet at T10?
author_version.justification: s1-s3: each same-as pair is judged by its stated names (holds 1, ID-1), timelessly (ID-3, SD-CAU-7); each has one system attestation, accepted by the system as its own claim (fixture-format acceptance), so holds True with that attestation as support (holds evidence table, established case). x14 is recorded after before-denial and so is invisible (common 0.2 as_of). s4: the established group of d1 is {d1,d2,d3,d4} through accepted links merged transitively (v0.2 3.1; common 0.2 identity); no pair in it is denied or disputed at this knowledge time, so ID-5 does not apply and the group is merged (holds 4: identity follows ID-2 to ID-8). member-of(d1,fleet-north), member-of(d2,...) and member-of(d4,...) are then semantically equivalent (v0.2 4.2). The accepted assertions m4 (from T2) and m2 (from T3) and the system-accepted denial m1d (from T2) all certainly hold at T10, so a polarity conflict on equivalent contents makes the answer DISPUTED with holds None (v0.2 5.3 rules; holds 3). support holds the deciding assertions and denials; by P-HO-1 the assertions m4, m2 are supporting and the accepted denial m1d is conflicting. The same-as links relied on for the merge are not added to s4's evidence (holds 4, ID-D 3.10); they appear only as support of s1-s3.
